newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NALCO to set up gallium plant.
newsitem.headline: India's NALCO to set up gallium plant.

text.p: India's state-run National Aluminium Company Ltd (NALCO) said on Saturday the mines ministry had approved its proposal to set up a gallium extraction plant in the eastern state of Orissa.

The statement said the plant, to be built at an estimated cost of 94.6 million rupees ($2.64 million), will be set up at NALCO's alumina refinery at Damanjodi, 525 km (344 miles) south of the state capital, Bhubaneshwar.
Out of the estimated cost, NALCO will provide 53.5 million rupees and the remaining amount will be provided by the federal government as grants, the statement said.
The project is expected to be completed in 18 months.
The statement said NALCO on Friday signed a technology transfer agreement with the National Research and Development Centre (NRDC) for the proposed project.

The project is considered important as gallium is used for electronic equipment, semi-conductors, space applications, light emitting diodes, lasers, super conducting magnets and high current switches, the statement said.
"The project will also make the country self-sufficient in the strategic metal," it said
NALCO, Asia's largest aluminium maker, produced 192,288 tonnes of aluminium in 1995/96 (April-March) against 178,072 tonnes in the previous year.
It has a domestic market share of 35 percent.
The company hopes to achieve a net profit of 5.1 billion rupees in 1996/97 against 5.4 billion in the previous year.
